translation_status stays draft: the translation was NOT proved by the driver. It transpiles (`python -m ldpy -t`), and its four reads were checked outside the pair, in a scratch module, against the original idioms on a hand-built report graph (results, a sh:conforms with a free subject, rdfs:label per result incl. a missing label, shui:conforms false incl. neighbours true / the plain string "false"): identical values.

Translation: `@graph report` after the export; report.subjects(RDF.type, SH.ValidationResult) -> m{ ?s a sh:ValidationResult }; report.objects(predicate=SH.conforms) (free subject) -> m{ [] sh:conforms ?o }; report.value(result, RDFS.label) -> m{ {result} rdfs:label ?l }.first(); report.subjects(SHUI.conforms, Literal(False, datatype=XSD.boolean)) -> m{ ?s shui:conforms false }. The other namespace uses (EX.carol, SH.Violation, XSD.float, ...) are prefixed names inside assertions, not reads; EX and SHUI become @prefix declarations of the module.

PITFALL found in the mechanical draft: `f"^^<{XSD.float}>"` became `f"^^<{xsd:float}>"`, which Python reads as the value `xsd` formatted with the spec `float` -- a silent runtime error, not a transpile error (no island is recognised inside an f-string field). Rewritten as `"^^<" + str(xsd:float) + ">"`.
